subject: Dedicated capacity staging plan & regional fallbacks
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Moore <evan@stellara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity staging plan & regional fallbacks

Hi Evan —

Great to meet on the call earlier. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass staging plan for the Dedicated (GPU pool) onboarding so your engineering and procurement teams have a clear checklist. High level:

- Recommended primary pool: us-west-2 (8xA100 baseline, 0.5 tokens/sec per GPU estimate at current model mix)
- Burst policy: scale to 20 GPUs for bursts up to 15 minutes, cold-start fallback to a smaller compatible model if queue > 60s
- Regional fallback: hot-standby pool in us-east-1 (4 GPUs) with automated routing on sustained latency > 200ms or instance preemption
- Autoscaling triggers: queue length, 90th-percentile request latency, and scheduled traffic windows (you can override)

Attachments: SOW_Stellara_v0.3.pdf, gpu_pool_config.yml, redwood-dedicated-bursting-matrix.xlsx

Notes / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm regulatory/regional constraints for any PHI traffic (we currently plan to isolate PHI to us-west only)?
2) What is your expected 95th pctl latency target for text-generation requests?
3) Proposed canary cutover window: Tue Nov 2, 02:00–06:00 PT — does that work for your ops team?

Next steps: if you sign off on the regional plan we’ll circulate an updated SOW and a DocuSign envelope for signatures. Marissa will own implementation runbooks and will coordinate the cutover.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-1203

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs

Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity staging plan & regional fallbacks

Thanks Aisha — quick follow-ups: 

- PHI: yes, any patient-identifiable traffic must remain in us-west for now. We can evaluate expanding to us-east later but need a formal security exception.
- Latency: our consumer-facing flow requires sub-200ms P95 for |prompt| < 1k tokens; internal analytics can tolerate higher. Will that be feasible with the baseline you suggested?
- Procurement: forwarding to procure@stellara.io — they’ll need the SOW + pricing sheet and prefer consolidated billing via PO.

Also: can you include an SLA paragraph that covers burst-induced throttling and what fallback behavior we should expect (queueing vs. model degradation)?

Appreciate the plan — Evan
Evan Moore
CTO, Stellara Health
ev@stellara.io

On Mon, Oct 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM Evan Moore <evan@stellara.io> wrote:
> Thanks Aisha — quick follow-ups:
> - PHI: yes, any patient-identifiable traffic must remain in us-west for now.
> - Latency: our consumer-facing flow requires sub-200ms P95 for |prompt| < 1k tokens; internal analytics can tolerate higher.
> - Procurement: forwarding to procure@stellara.io — they’ll need the SOW + pricing sheet and prefer consolidated billing via PO.
>
Thanks — noted on all three. Short answers here and I’ll add detail in the SOW update:

- PHI: we’ll gate PHI traffic to the us-west pool; routing rule will tag requests by tenant header and force us-west routing. We’ll document the header and sample proxy config in the runbook.
- Latency: with the proposed baseline (8xA100) we expect P95 ~ 160–210ms depending on prompt distribution; that’s why we recommend the burst capacity and the hot-standby. If you need a tighter P95 target we can bump baseline or deploy quantized variants for predictable lower-latency tails.
- SLA / fallback: we will add an explicit SLA paragraph: during defined burst windows we guarantee routing to dedicated pool; if bursts exceed burst capacity, automatic fallback is to a smaller compatible model (same safety filters) with a published expected quality delta and a backlog queue with max wait 120s before fallback.

I attached an updated SOW draft (v0.3) and gpu_pool_config.yml that makes the routing and tagging explicit. Marissa will follow up with a technical runbook and a proposed on-call schedule.

If procurement needs a PO flow we can provide consolidated billing terms and a procurement contact (Rishi) to help with counters.

Best,
Aisha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Moore <evan@stellara.io>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity staging plan & regional fallbacks

Hi all — adding implementation notes from the delivery side so Stellara has the operational picture.

Key runbook excerpts (attached full runbook in Drive):
- Cutover steps (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m stabilization windows between phases. Rollback on sustained error rate > 2% for 15m.
- Monitoring: we’ll provision per-route dashboards (token-level cost, P95 latency, error rate) and a synthetic probe hitting representative prompts every 5 minutes.
- Scaling policy: autoscaler will add 2 GPUs per scale event, cooldown 3m, burst cap hard limit 20 GPUs. If queue persists for >5m and we've hit hard cap we trigger model-fallback policy.
- On-call: Redwood on-call (pager): +1-650-555-0199. Stellara on-call contact requested for cutover; please confirm name/number.

Action items for Stellara before canary:
1) Confirm PHI routing header and share a sample request (JSON) we can test against the staging pool.
2) Confirm maintenance blackout windows and escalate contacts.
3) Procurement signoff on SOW v0.3 (Aisha + Rishi to coordinate).

I’ll schedule a 30-minute dry-run with your infra team the week before cutover. Proposed dry-run: Mon Nov 1, 09:00 PT.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
